text:
jordan (support): hey team — customer reported streaming responses get cut off mid-event when requests flow through a gRPC->HTTP1 gateway. they see partial SSE frames, then the connection closes, client reconnects and gets a new session. happens ~30% of requests, more common with longer outputs. example curl they used:

curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N "https://gateway.customer.example/stream?session=abc123"

jordan (support): customer says if they hit our hosted endpoint directly (no gateway) streaming is fine. only fails when gateway/proxy is in path. they attached a short capture of the raw bytes — looks like last chunk/line never reaches client.

alex (eng-runtime): that smells like an intermediary converting h2 -> h1 and switching to chunked buffering rules. common causes: 1) upstream not sending Transfer-Encoding: chunked + no Content-Length -> some proxies buffer until EOF, 2) proxy buffering enabled (nginx default), 3) gateway doing gRPC translation that waits for flush boundary.

alex (eng-runtime): can you get us a minimal repro curl that uses http2 explicitly? e.g.

# try HTTP/2 directly, no buffering
curl --http2 -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://gateway.customer.example/stream?session=abc123"

ingrid (infra): logging request/response flow. please run nghttp for a real h2 trace:

nghttp -v -n 1 "https://gateway.customer.example/stream?session=abc123"

ingrid (infra): also asked customer to capture tcpdump on their side (client -> gateway) and we can capture on our edge. need to confirm whether RST_STREAM is coming from gateway or from our runtime.

maria (platform): note — our runtime flushes partial tokens as SSE data chunks and relies on downstream supporting streaming without added buffering. if the gateway inserts a content-length or groups chunks we get coalesced frames and sometimes the proxy closes early when it thinks stream ended.

ben (sre): saw similar issue last quarter with an Envoy config that had http1 codec buffering enabled. for Envoy -> upstream HTTP/1.1 you need to set "use_remote_address"/codec options and enable streaming by turning off http1 request/response buffering. minimal envoy snippet we used:```
- name: envoy.filters.http.router
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.router.v3.Router
    start_child_span: true
# and at the upstream cluster level
upstream_http_protocol_options:
  auto_sni: true
  allow_chunked_length: true
```
ben (sre): also check cluster.settings: max_response_bytes and whether early EOF is enforced.

jordan (support): customer sent an excerpt of edge access logs — pasted below (redacted):

"GET /stream?session=abc123 200 12ms upstream_response_time=0.18 body_bytes_sent=1024"
"GET /stream?session=abc456 200 1ms upstream_response_time=0.03 body_bytes_sent=512 RST_STREAM"

jordan (support): they saw RST_STREAM after ~2-3s for the failing ones.

alex (eng-runtime): RST_STREAM could be either side. if the gateway sees long-lived connection and a health check / idle timeout closes it, you'll get abrupt cutoff. check keepalive and idle timeouts on proxies. for nginx:

proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";

alex (eng-runtime): also confirm the gateway does not rewrite chunked framing. Some gRPC HTTP transcoding layers will buffer until they can form a complete gRPC message then flush; for token-level streaming that's too coarse.

maria (platform): quick repro we can run internally — create a small client that connects to our edge via a simple HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy vs direct h2. I can spin up a local nginx with default config and an envoy that proxies h2->h1 to our runtime to reproduce. asking for a concrete failing curl + headers capture from customer.

jordan (support): customer provided full request headers (redacted):
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Accept: text/event-stream
User-Agent: MyClient/1.2
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate

jordan (support): they say Content-Length not present (expected).

ingrid (infra): next steps for triage:
- collect tcpdump on our edge for failing request (we have capture id CAP-20260312-37)
- enable debug logs on gateway host for 30m
- ask customer to run curl --http2 --no-buffer and supply verbose output

dev-proxy-bot: canary deploy of gateway v2.7.1 to staging completed :white_check_mark: (sha abcdef)

alex (eng-runtime): additional repro command that helped us in the past (shows raw event boundary):

# raw socket read in python, prints chunks as received
python - <<'PY'
import sys, requests
for chunk in requests.get('https://gateway.customer.example/stream?session=abc123', stream=True).iter_lines():
    print('RECV:', chunk)
PY

maria (platform): if customer can flip nginx proxy_buffering off and proxy_http_version to 1.1 it often fixes SSE behavior. for Envoy we set "allow_chunked_length: true" and disable http1 buffering. we'll draft exact config snippets to share.

ben (sre): also check TLS terminator (LB) idle timeouts. some LBs proxy HTTP/2 on front and HTTP/1.1 to backend with aggressive idle timeout, closing if no bytes forwarded for N secs. streaming with small token cadence may appear idle. increase idle to 60s for testing.

jordan (support): customer asked if this is a known issue with gRPC gateways and SSE — reply: yes, intermediary translation layers often cause buffering or boundary grouping. we're going to: (1) collect tcpdump + nghttp traces, (2) try repro with local nginx/envoy, (3) provide recommended proxy config and a short patch to our docs for customers using gRPC transcoding.

ingrid (infra): assigning CAP-20260312-37 to infra, enabling gateway debug 30m window now. will paste logs when we have them. ETA 2h.

alex (eng-runtime): follow-on: if we confirm gateway is closing with RST_STREAM on us, we should add more robust resume semantics in the client (session resume) and improve our runtime to gracefully handle mid-stream reconnects by preserving some context where possible. that's longer term.

jordan (support): thanks. I'll ping customer with an ask to run the --http2 --no-buffer curl and to temporarily disable proxy_buffering (if they control gateway) or increase idle timeouts. will update thread with captures. :thumbsup:
